verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents an official Docker Compose self-host (MongoDB, API, front-end) and calls itself open source. A hands-on probe booted the official image and completed a keyless flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license. Evaluation data stays local: the SDKs evaluate in memory and never send attribute values to GrowthBook, and a self-hosted Proxy can cache payloads on your own infrastructure. Missing for 10: clarity on whether paid-tier capabilities (SSO/SCIM, audit logs, approval workflows) are included in the open-source self-hosted distribution, and a documented non-Docker install path.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Open Source Feature Flags, Experimentation, and Product Analytics
a real flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license.
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
Run the GrowthBook Proxy next to your app to cache SDK payloads, reduce latency, and keep serving flags if the API is down.
We have used the self-hosted version a few months in my company now, and are very happy about it.
